title: Little Hanuman and the sun.
lines: Long ago, in India, there lived a very special little monkey.
And that's why Hanuman could do something no other monkey could do: he could fly!
Hanuman was very strong and very fast, but he was also still very small, and a bit naughty.
Mummy had gone out for a moment to look for fruit.
Hanuman looked out of the window.
And there, in the sky, he saw something lovely.
He jumped as high as he could, and he flew up.
Higher and higher, past the trees, past the mountains, past the birds and through the clouds.
Hanuman flew closer and closer to the sun.
Pff, what a warm mango, said Hanuman.
The sun saw the little monkey coming and had to laugh.
Little monkey, I'm not a mango!
If you eat me, it will be dark everywhere, and then nobody will be able to see anything.
The flowers can't grow, and the children can't play outside.
He got such a fright that he bumped his chin on a cloud.
His chin got a little swollen and round.
Hanuman floated slowly down, as gently as a feather, because the wind, his daddy, caught him.
I wanted to eat the sun, Mummy.
I thought it was a mango!
Mummy had to laugh, and she gave him a big hug.
Here, this is a real mango.
And Hanuman ate a tasty, sweet, real mango.
From that day on Hanuman had a round little chin.
And you know, in the old Indian language Hanu means: chin.
Hanuman, the monkey with the brave chin!
When Hanuman grew up, he became Prince Rama's strongest and kindest helper.
People also call him Mahavir, the great hero.
But he always stayed a little naughty, and he always kept loving mangoes.
